name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CVE-2025-61624 — Fortinet Multiple Products Path Traversal Vulnerability
items.dek: Fortinet Multiple Products. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 19 October.

items.title: CVE-2026-102764 — BeyondTrust Remote Support Authentication Bypass by Spoofing Vulnerability
items.dek: BeyondTrust Remote Support. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 19 October.

items.title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale
items.dek: 16.4% of MCP servers expose filesystem capabilities beyond their declared contract; dynamic evaluation confirms 150 exploitable instances across registries.
items.unproven: whether the vulnerability manifests in production deployments where agents run with restricted filesystem permissions by policy or container isolation

items.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards
items.dek: Agent safety guards shift verdicts on translated requests; smaller and purpose-built models flip decisions beyond noise floor, with flips rising to +4.4pp on rare languages.
items.unproven: whether the effect propagates to code-switching or hybrid requests, or whether guard vendors have since addressed language-dependent brittleness

items.title: Combining LLM and Dynamic Analysis for Universal Testing of Static Application Security Testing Tools
items.dek: LLM4SAST detected 66 unique faults in SAST tools by generating code variants and comparing tool reports using metamorphic relations.
items.unproven: Evaluated on unspecified SAST tools and programming languages; unclear whether faults are representative of production tooling the reader uses.

items.title: ExecWeave: Cross-Layer Execution Provenance for Observable Agentic Software
items.dek: System to correlate agent actions across application traces and OS telemetry with explicit uncertainty tracking; directly applicable to securing agentic SDLC audit.
items.unproven: proof-of-concept implementation; no measurement of false-positive or false-negative rates on real agent codebases; bounded search for command-to-process correlation admits unprovable associations.

items.title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
items.dek: Twelve attacks on agent step-up authorization; audit of ten runtimes finds no third-party approval record and post-approval argument changes in four of eight; reference defense (ASU) with Tamarin proofs.
items.unproven: reference design not yet deployed; 27,108 scripted trials and 609 AgentDojo tests do not cover all agent platforms or approval workflows; fixes require runtime or protocol changes the reader may not control.

items.title: CVE-2026-21589 — Atlassian Multiple Products Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties Vulnerability
items.dek: Atlassian Multiple Products. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 18 October.

items.title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming
items.dek: Red-teaming pipeline synthesizes edited agent transcripts to evade action-only monitors; six attacks bypassed a frontier developer's monitor.
items.unproven: whether attacks generalize to other developers' monitoring; scale and payload sophistication relative to real adversaries

items.title: Thinking in Graphs: Neo4j-Backed Exploit-Chain Reasoning for LLM Penetration-Testing Agents
items.dek: ChainGraph externalizes multi-step attack reasoning into Neo4j, enabling agents to rank exploit chains by combined severity and identify chokepoints.
items.unproven: performance on real penetration tests; generalization beyond Active Directory scenarios; whether chain-severity scoring correlates with business risk

items.title: CoRedSkill: Stealthy Skill Composition Attacks via AST-Guided Injection
items.dek: AST-guided injection embeds undetectable attacks across agent skills while preserving individual utility; 98% success, 3.3% detection rate.
items.unproven: evaluated only on constructed 150-case benchmark; generalization to production agent architectures and real skill repositories undemonstrated.

items.title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains
items.dek: Independent Verifiability Rate of quantized GGUF models is 0/198 on Hugging Face; floating-point contraction and quantization recipe must be disclosed to reproduce.
items.unproven: whether disclosure becomes standard practice; adoption by model providers; impact on supply chain trust workflows.

items.title: Beyond Maliciousness: Static and Runtime Attack-Surface Profiling of Agent Skills
items.dek: 70% of agent skills in two marketplaces expose shell execution or elevated capabilities with no user-visible permission model.
items.unproven: methodology applies to skills as static artifacts; does not model capability drift across agent model versions or prompt-injection attacks that bypass skill design

items.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
items.dek: Evaluation datasets for agent safety guards contain dataset shortcuts predicting labels; guard performance degrades sharply under domain holdout or balanced weighting.
items.unproven: whether the audit framework detects shortcuts in newly released benchmarks, or whether disclosed findings have prompted benchmark redesign

items.title: What Survives Self-Evolution: Provenance Marks in Copied Agent Harnesses
items.dek: Published provenance marks in agent harnesses survive LLM self-evolution attacks at low rates (0–42%); order-based marks detected in 82% of rewritten copies.
items.unproven: whether the proposed order-based mark survives attacks at scale beyond held-out test games; robustness against adversaries targeting the mark specifically

items.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation in S3-Compatible Object Storage under Client Concurrency
items.dek: ML-KEM encryption of S3 objects incurs 4.0–4.9% throughput loss only under client CPU saturation; software calling patterns account for most overhead.
items.unproven: generalizability beyond tested S3-compatible stores and processor types; cost under realistic financial services workload profiles and concurrency patterns

items.title: Evaluating and Improving Static Application Security Testing Tools for Rust
items.dek: Rust SAST tools show systematic weaknesses on real-world vulnerabilities; LLM-assisted mutation testing framework (TRUST) automatically generates test cases.
items.unproven: whether TRUST detects gaps the reader's current SAST configuration misses; applicability to unsafe code patterns in their codebase

items.title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation
items.dek: LLM-based agent evaluators cannot detect deployment tampering or runtime substitution; benchmark shows 88–94% acceptance of tampered outputs.
items.unproven: laboratory setting with synthetic tampers; no evidence this applies to production evaluation pipelines or what fraction of evaluations this reader's firm actually runs; manifest-hash proposal untested.

items.title: Quantum-Aware Key Rank for Side-Channel Attacks evaluation
items.dek: Quantum-aware key rank metric models post-quantum cryptanalysis of block ciphers with quadratic advantage collapsing beyond rank 2^58.6 under NIST depth.
items.unproven: Practical exploitation path; applicability to ciphers outside AES-128; confirmation that actual quantum hardware will achieve the theoretical speedup.

items.title: Quiet Triggers, Loud Footprints: A Tri-Space Measurement Study of Backdoor Stealthiness
items.dek: Tri-space measurement framework reveals backdoor attacks quiet in one space are loud in others; no attack achieves consistent stealthiness.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to image classification; applicability to other domains and defenses beyond those tested undemonstrated.

items.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks on Flow-Based Intrusion Detection
items.dek: 0.001% training-data poisoning implants undetectable backdoors in flow-based IDS; diagnostic methodology localizes triggers and enables mitigation.
items.unproven: evaluated on single dataset and model family; applicability to production IDS deployments and diverse network architectures undemonstrated.
